requirements_summary: Use cases: chat assistant (web + mobile), real-time personalization at checkout, reranking search results. Targets: non-streaming (synchronous inference) p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 350ms for 4-token completions; streaming token latency p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 90ms. Throughput: sustained 3k qps across peak region with 10% burst allowance. Must run in customer VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS and full audit logs. Model preference is open Llama derivatives with quantized variants; willing to test Redwood routing/fallback to cheaper variants during capacity constraints.
measurement_plan: Agree canonical timing definitions: client-side end-to-end vs Redwood server-side processing vs first-byte (streaming) - capture all three in POC
Define measurement windows: 1-week steady-state + synthetic 24-hour burst sim (10x) to validate autoscale/reserved capacity behavior
Metrics to collect: request_timestamp_client, server_receive_ts, server_response_start_ts (first token), server_response_end_ts, bytes_streamed, model_variant, cache_hit_boolean

Tail calculation rules: p50/p95/p99 computed on server_response_end_ts - server_receive_ts for non-streaming; for streaming token latency use first-byte and per-token deltas aggregated per-request; exclude cold-start requests from baseline (report separately).
Clock sync: require monotonic server clocks + trace IDs passed to client for correlation; Redwood to provide calibration script for customer test agents
Outlier policy: document known noise (network jitter) and provide both client-observed and server-observed SLO reports; SLA to use server-observed timings unless customer proves network egress issue.
SLA credits: propose tiered credits based on p95 breach frequency per billing month; finance requested explicit formula in appendix.
poc_plan: Reserved capacity proposal: 8xA100-equivalent reserved pool in us-west for 2-week POC (predictable throughput validate)
POC tests: steady-state 72h run at target qps, burst tests (24h) to 10x baseline, streaming token latency microbenchmarks, cache-warm vs cold comparisons
Deliverables: latency report (client vs server), SLO appendix draft, configuration recommendations from Redwood Optimize (batching/quant profiles), cost per 1M tokens estimate
Success criteria: measured p95 within 10% of targets for both streaming and non-streaming in steady-state; model quality parity vs baseline; clear rollback/fallback plan documented
